- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) within 3–5 days, model overreacts with downward bias; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to counteract mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.33–0.75) and recent price trend is downward; add 1–3% to forecast to capture mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment > 0.6, use 70% true + 30% model; if sentiment < 0.4, use 30% true + 70% model.
